title: Podcast EP357: How Gonka is Changing the Way AI is Accessed with David Liberman - Semiwiki
gist: A 19-minute SemiWiki podcast blurb on Gonka, a decentralized protocol connecting buyers of AI compute with GPU hardware operators as an open alternative to centralized cloud for inference and training. The headline assertion relayed from co-creator David Liberman is that Bitcoin's decentralized infrastructure exceeds the combined infrastructures of AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OpenAI and SpaceX, and that applying the same techniques to AI produces the most efficient and cost-effective AI infrastructure available today.

insights.claim: Gonka is a decentralized protocol that matches parties needing AI computing power with operators supplying GPU hardware, positioned as an open alternative to centralized cloud providers for both inference and model training.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Decentralized GPU marketplaces are a tail risk to hyperscaler inference pricing power — worth tracking whether any achieves real utilization, not just token issuance.
insights.quote: Gonka is a decentralized protocol that connects people who need computing power for AI with operators who provide GPU hardware.
insights.locator: Daniel is joined by David Liberman

insights.claim: The design debate underpinning Gonka is proof-of-stake versus proof-of-work as applied to decentralized compute infrastructure, treating consensus mechanism choice as a compute-infrastructure question rather than a purely financial one.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: How a compute network secures itself determines whether operator incentives survive a token drawdown — the key diligence axis for decentralized-compute projects.
insights.quote: He begins with a discussion of proof-of-stake vs. proof-of-work as applied to decentralized compute infrastructure.
insights.locator: In this compelling and far-reaching discussion

insights.claim: David Liberman claims Bitcoin's decentralized infrastructure is larger than the combined infrastructures of AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OpenAI and SpaceX, using it as evidence that decentralized coordination can outbuild centralized capex.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: An extraordinary comparison that conflates specialized ASIC hash capacity with general-purpose cloud capacity — the kind of claim to stress-test before underwriting any decentralized-compute thesis.
insights.quote: Bitcoin was built with a decentralized approach and David explains that the resulting infrastructure is larger the combined infrastructures of AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OpenAI, and SpaceX.
insights.locator: In this discussion, David explains the power of a decentralized community

insights.claim: The argument advanced is that applying Bitcoin-style decentralized techniques to AI yields the most efficient and cost-effective AI infrastructure in the world today — a present-tense claim, not a forecast.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If decentralized inference were already cheapest, it would show up in hyperscaler inference pricing; the absence of that evidence is the test of the claim.
insights.quote: When these decentralized techniques are applied to AI, the result is the most efficient and cost-effective infrastructure for using AI in the world today.
insights.locator: When these decentralized techniques are applied to AI

insights.claim: Gonka's co-creator David Liberman is a Los Angeles-based futurist, serial entrepreneur, investor and former Director of Products at Snap — a consumer-product rather than infrastructure background.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Founder background matters for infrastructure protocols; consumer-product provenance raises execution questions on datacenter-grade reliability.
insights.locator: Daniel is joined by David Liberman
